hints: Focus on the shape around each carbon, as double-bonded carbons are flat while single-bonded carbons are tetrahedral.
Notice that molecule 1 has a C=C core with four methyl carbons attached, and molecule 2 has only three carbons in total.
Remember that any three points define a plane, but a puckered ring cannot be flattened, then check which combination fits.
walkthrough:
**Recall planarity rules**

Think like this. A $C=C$ double bond is trigonal planar, so the two $sp^2$ carbons plus the four atoms directly attached to them all sit in one flat plane.

In contrast, $sp^3$ single-bonded carbons are tetrahedral, so long chains and rings can twist out of plane.

**Check molecule 1**

2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene is $(CH_3)_2C=C(CH_3)_2$.

$$C_2 = C_3 \text{ with four } CH_3 \text{ groups attached}$$
The central $C=C$ is flat, and all four methyl carbons are bonded directly to those $sp^2$ carbons, so all six carbons lie in the same plane. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check molecule 2**

Propane is $CH_3-CH_2-CH_3$ with only three carbon atoms.

Any three points in space always define a plane, so the three carbons must be coplanar even though each carbon is tetrahedral. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check molecule 3 and conclude**

Cyclohexane, $C_6H_{12}$, is not flat. It puckers into chair and boat conformations to reduce strain, so its six carbons do not lie in one plane. Statement 3 is incorrect.

Therefore only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: This option includes 1, 2 and 3. Statements 1 and 2 are correct, but 3 is wrong because cyclohexane adopts a puckered chair shape, not a flat hexagon, so not all its carbons are coplanar.
options.B: This option includes 1 and 2 only. This is correct because the six carbons of (CH3)2C=C(CH3)2 are held in the trigonal planar system of the double bond, and the three carbons of propane must define a single plane.
options.C: This option includes 2 and 3 only. Statement 2 is correct, but it wrongly includes cyclohexane and wrongly leaves out 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, whose C=C unit makes all its carbons planar.
options.D: This option includes 1 only. Statement 1 is correct, but it wrongly leaves out propane. Students sometimes think tetrahedral carbons cannot be planar, forgetting that any three atoms always lie in the same plane.
